label: EdgeRouter 12P

poe.note: Ubiquiti prints no total PoE budget on either surface. The tech-spec page states the PoE interface ((10) 24V passive PoE ports, 2-pair (Pins 4, 5+; 7, 8-)), the included 60 W (24 V, 2.5 A) AC/DC adapter, "Max. power consumption 20 W (excluding PoE output)" and "Passive PoE Max. wattage per port: 17 W (24 V)". The 40 W recorded here is the arithmetic of that stated configuration - 60 W adapter minus 20 W of device draw leaves 40 W for the passive ports - and is an envelope derived from two printed figures, not a budget Ubiquiti prints. A lab that fits a larger DC supply inside the 9-30 V range can declare its own.

notes: Vendor figures from Ubiquiti own tech-spec page (read 2026-11-19, HTTP 200, 575,620 B): Networking interface **(10) 10/100/1000 RJ45 ports, (2) 1 Gbps SFP ports**; PoE interface **(10) 24V passive PoE ports, 2-pair (Pins 4, 5+; 7, 8-)**; Power method **AC/DC power adapter, 60W, 24V DC, 2.5A (Included)**; Supported voltage range **9-30V DC**; Max. power consumption **20W (Excludes PoE output)**; Passive PoE Max. wattage per port **17W (24V)**; Passive PoE voltage range **20-30V**. store.ui.com/us/en/products/er-12p (200, 323,284 B) corroborates. No datasheet: dl.ui.com/ds/er-12p_ds.pdf answers 302 to the techspecs root and dl.ui.com/qig/er-12p answers 302 there too, so every figure above is tech-spec-only. This box is 2-pair passive only - it cannot feed a 4-pair 802.3at PD, so the port class is passive, not PoE+.
